Native extensions may release interpreter locks, so choose a design from the actual workload rather than assuming all Python CPU work behaves identically.

spoken: Concurrency allows work to overlap in progress, while parallelism executes work at the same time on available compute resources. A bounded queue limits admitted waiting work. Neither a task count nor an unbounded queue is a capacity guarantee: include active work, queue age, deadlines and downstream limits in the system budget.

Q: Why must resources be cleaned up on cancellation as well as on ordinary failure?
spoken: Cancellation changes control flow while a task may own files, queue items or locks. Use structured cleanup such as finally and context managers, and propagate cancellation after restoring owned invariants. A cleanup operation may itself need a bounded protected phase, but shielding unlimited work can make shutdown hang.

Q: How do processes, threads and shared memory change failure isolation?
spoken: Threads normally share a process address space, while processes provide a separate address-space boundary and require explicit communication or shared-memory arrangements. Processes can isolate some crashes and scale independent work, but add startup, serialization and coordination costs. Neither choice automatically prevents data races or secures untrusted code.

Q: How do a timeout and a deadline differ across a multi-step operation?

Propagate a single deadline and derive each remaining wait from it, while leaving time for cleanup and a truthful outcome.
